items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: It was Andy Burns, who grew up in Clinton, was good friends with Jim Ball, who grew up in Clinton, and Andy was my second cousin’s roommate... I met them at a party in New York

ctx.x: Well at the time there was — I don’t think there was much of an opportunity to go and study how to be a recording engineer. Now you have Full Sail Recording School, and most music schools have programs for that. Was apprenticeship something that you aspired to?

Yeah, that was really the only way to do it, and the bigger studios had a system in place for training people. And at the time it was — Record Plant and Power Station were the two biggest studios in New York. They were cranking out all the hits that you’d be hearing at the time. And I had met, now a good friend of mine, Jim Ball, through like a convoluted thing, which, everybody’s contacts always come through some kind of convoluted thing. It was Andy Burns, who grew up in Clinton, was good friends with Jim Ball,…
How did you pay your rent?
